subject: Model improvement prohibition & KMS segregation — DPA addendum request
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@healthinnovate.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@healthinnovate.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA addendum: model improvement prohibition + key separation

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this on. We've attached our redlines to the DPA (HealthInnovate_DPA_redlines.pdf). Two items that are blocking legal sign-off on our side:

1) A firm no-model-improvement ("no-train") commitment for customer interaction data used by our product. We need an explicit clause that: "Redwood will not use HealthInnovate production inputs or outputs to improve model weights or create derivative models without prior written consent."

2) Operational proof that keys and plaintext are segregated: HealthInnovate requires KMS segregation (separate key material and onshore key wrapping) for any logs that leave our environment for telemetry or debugging. We also need a list of subprocessors with access to raw transcripts and their access purpose.

Can you confirm Redwood can: (a) accept the no-train language as redlined, (b) provide an operations attestation for KMS segregation and subprocessor list, and (c) share an export-friendly one-page runbook for our security team?

If easier, we can do a 30-min call this week — cc'd contracts for scheduling.

Best,
Alex Mercer\VP Security, HealthInnovate

Attachments: HealthInnovate_DPA_redlines.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@healthinnovate.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@healthinnovate.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA addendum: model improvement prohibition + key separation

Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redlines. High level answers up front:

- No-train: Redwood is prepared to accept a targeted no-model-improvement clause for HealthInnovate production interactions (we call this a "no-adaptive-training" commitment). We typically implement this as a contractual commitment plus operational exclusions to ensure logs are not routed into model training pipelines.

- KMS segregation & onshore wrapping: we can offer customer-managed keys (CMK) with a dedicated key ring for HealthInnovate and an onshore key-wrapping option in the US region. We will provide an attestation snapshot and a one-page ops runbook describing encryption, key rotation, and how we scoping logs for debugging.

- Subprocessors: I will share the current subprocessors list and a short note on why each has access. If HealthInnovate needs tighter gating, we can propose contractual limiting language and an approval workflow for new subprocessors.

Request for next steps: can you confirm the exact redline wording you want for the no-train paragraph? If you prefer, we can propose a clause and call it out in the addendum. Also tagging David and Kimberly on ops/procurement: David, Kimberly — can you prepare (1) a 1-page ops runbook we can send to HealthInnovate, (2) a current subprocessors list with access scopes, and (3) an attestation template we can execute?

Happy to take a quick call this week — my calendar is open Wed/Thu morning PST.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: HealthInnovate asks (DPA redlines + KMS segregation) — need artifacts

David/Kim — quick internal note following the HealthInnovate redlines (attached in the thread). They want three artifacts:

1) A short contractual clause we can accept for no-model-improvement. They prefer explicit language: "Redwood will not use HealthInnovate production inputs or outputs to improve model weights, fine-tune models, or create derivative models without the Customer's prior written consent."

2) Ops evidence of key/material segregation: specifically they asked for (a) confirmation of a dedicated key ring/KMS namespace for HealthInnovate, (b) confirmation that any backup or telemetry that includes plaintext is either removed or encrypted with the customer key, and (c) an onshore wrapping option in the US region.

3) Subprocessor roster with access purpose (who can see raw transcripts, who can see derived metrics, who can only see telemetry). If a subprocessors snapshot is not current, please include the last audit date.

Deliverables requested:
- One-page ops runbook (PDF) we can send externally (sensitive detail redacted).
- Attestation template (short statement + audit snapshot link).
- Proposed addendum language for legal to review (I can loop Legal once we have wording).

Timeline: they'd like these by EOD tomorrow PST if possible to keep procurement moving. If that's tight, flag what you need.

Thanks — Hannah

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@healthinnovate.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA addendum: model improvement prohibition + key separation

Hannah / Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick operational confirmation and next steps:

- KMS segregation: We will provision a dedicated key ring for HealthInnovate in the US region and can support customer-managed keys (CMK). Keys used for storing customer interaction logs will be separate from our control-plane keys. We will provide a snapshot of the key ring and an auditable access list (redwood-kms-segregation-summary.pdf).

- No-model-improvement controls: We'll implement a data-routing tag (customer:healthinnovate, policy:no_train) at the ingestion layer so HealthInnovate traffic is excluded from model training pipelines and downstream experiment buckets. We will also add a logging flag documenting excluded datasets.

- Subprocessors: Attached is the current subprocessors roster with access purposes (included in the Drive link). We will include the last audit date for each subprocess. If HealthInnovate needs per-subprocessor approval, we can propose a 14-day review SLA for new additions.

Deliverables (attached/linked):
- ops-runbook-healthinnovate-v1.docx (one-page runbook, safe-for-external).
- redwood-kms-segregation-summary.pdf (attestation snapshot).
- Drive folder with subprocessors roster and audit logs (link above).

Alex — please let us know if the proposed addendum language below matches what you need. If so, we'll draft formal wording and loop Legal.

Proposed language (informal):
"Redwood will not use Customer production inputs or outputs to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve machine learning models, or to create derivative models, without the Customer's prior written consent. Redwood will implement operational controls to exclude Customer-tagged data from model training pipelines and will provide an attestation of implemented controls upon Customer request."

If that's acceptable, Hannah can loop Legal and Contracts to convert into DPA text.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Director, Reliability & Security Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-kms-segregation-summary.pdf; ops-runbook-healthinnovate-v1.docx
